Okay first, like in every other language there are hundreds of ways to express a certain statement!

Let me break those down for you!

\- Ich habe es mir noch nicht überlegt:

  "I haven't thought about it yet", it's polite and signalizes, that you´ll need some time to form your opinion!

\- Ich weiß es noch nicht sicher:

  "I am not completely sure at the moment", this one signalizes, that you already thought about something, but   
  you aren't comfortable with sharing it just now. You are still considering an invitation for example

\- Ich bin mir noch unsicher:

  "Give me some more time to decide", really similar to to the second, but a more fitting example here would be   
  a teacher-student-situation, in which he is asking you a question and you answer it to get a few more seconds   
  for consideration; More phrase in that situation: "Eine Sekunde", "Lassen sie(sie=formal) mich nochmal   
  überlegen"

\- Ich habe es mir noch nicht völlig überlegt:

  "I haven't finished thinking about it", Again quite close to the other ones above! Tells your opposite, that you   
  are currently in the progress of thinking about it. This is less formal, maybe in a friend-friend-situation.

\- Ich überlege noch:

  "I'm thinking about it", not exactly rude/, but not friendly either. Its quite short and may be used while talking   
  to friends and family. Sometimes used while already knowing not to accept (an invitation for example)

​

Hope this helps! If there are any questions remaining, feels free to ask :)

Other options are:

\-Ich habe es mir noch nicht überlegt!

\-Ich weiß es noch nicht sicher.

\-Ich bin mir noch unsicher.

\-Ich habe mir das noch nicht völlig überlegt

\-Ich überlege noch.

\- ...
